name: Block disposable emails at signup (Email Verifier)

parameters.content:
# Real-time signup check

POST `{ "email": "someone@example.com" }` to this webhook. It answers:

```json
{ "decision": "allow" | "review" | "block", "reason": "...", "status": "...", "sub_status": "..." }
```

**block** — invalid syntax, dead domain, no such mailbox, or a disposable address
**review** — catch-all, role account, or a free provider whose mailbox cannot be confirmed
**allow** — SMTP confirmed the mailbox exists

## Setup (once)

**1. Get an Apify token** — https://console.apify.com/settings/integrations

**2. Create the n8n credential**
Credentials → New → **Header Auth**
- Name: `Apify API`
- Header name: `Authorization`
- Header value: `Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN`

Every HTTP node here already points at that credential by name. No token is stored in this file.

## One run per signup

This calls the Actor once per request, which suits a form. For a list, use the Google Sheets or CSV template instead — batching is far cheaper per address.

## Cost

Pay-per-event: one charge per address that gets a verdict, including undeliverable and unknown — the work was done either way. From $0.55 per 1,000, tiered by your Apify plan.

Current pricing: https://apify.com/sumitr_mardy/email-verifier/pricing

Actor: https://apify.com/sumitr_mardy/email-verifier
Templates & docs: https://github.com/sumitrmardy/email-verifier-api

## Change the policy here, not in the response node

The decision is one small block of JavaScript on purpose: your rules are not ours. A B2B product usually wants `role_based` allowed; a consumer app usually does not. A trial signup might accept `catch_all`; a paid plan might not.

`unknown` means the check could not complete — greylisting, a timeout. Blocking on `unknown` rejects real customers for a network hiccup, so it is `review` here.
